title: Writing Your First Python Program
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main behavior of writing your first python program.

Identify one limitation, edge case, compatibility concern, or failure mode relevant to the topic.

content.intro: This lesson introduces writing your first python program as part of python syntax, variables, and objects. It turns the curriculum heading into a short, practical concept guide with a visual, example, and checks to try locally.
content.why_it_matters: Writing Your First Python Program belongs to Python Syntax, Variables, and Objects. Focus on the specific rule it introduces, compare one correct example with a nearby edge case, and explain the difference in your own words.

content.task: Try it yourself: adapt the example to demonstrate writing your first python program with different inputs. Write down your prediction, run it locally, and explain the result plus one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the central idea in writing your first python program without copying the definition.
Run or manually verify the smallest example using the stated runtime assumptions.

hints: Read the sample carefully and identify the values or state that affect the result.
Change one variable or input at a time and predict what should happen before running it.
Check the official reference and runtime version if behavior differs from the expected result.
